course_name_original: Teoría de Circuitos y Máquinas Eléctricas

learning_outcomes.text: Students will know the basic quantities of circuit theory and electrical machines.
The resolution of circuits in sinusoidal steady-state with linear elements.
The power and energy balance in a single-phase circuit.
The power and energy balance in a three-phase circuit.
The operation of single-phase and three-phase transformers.
The operation of asynchronous motors and alternators.

syllabus_topics: Periodic signals. Alternating signals. Sinusoidal signals. Generation.
Mathematical representation of sinusoidal signals. Vector description: Phasors.
Behavior of basic components with sinusoidal signals. Impedance. Element association.
Circuit analysis: Fundamental laws and theorems.
Instantaneous power. Complex power. Power balance. Power triangle.
Power factor. Its importance in electrical energy supply. Correction.
General classification of electrical machines. Basic constructive elements. Losses in an electrical machine.
Magnetically coupled coils. Coupling coefficient. Ideal and real coupling.
Fundamentals of electromagnetic conversion.
Rated values and nameplate of a single-phase transformer.
Principle of operation of an ideal single-phase transformer.
Equivalent circuit of the real single-phase transformer.
Tests of the single-phase transformer: No-load and short-circuit.
Voltage drop in a single-phase transformer.
Efficiency in a single-phase transformer.
Generation of three-phase systems. Phase and sequence.
Star-delta connection. Voltage and current relationships.
Calculation of systems with balanced loads.
Power in balanced three-phase systems. Measurement.
Power factor correction in balanced three-phase systems.
Three-column three-phase transformer. Constructive aspects.
Connections of three-phase transformers. Hour index.
Tests of the three-phase transformer: No-load and short-circuit.
Analysis of the three-phase transformer.
Construction. Principle of operation (Asynchronous machine, Three-phase motor).
Ferraris' theorem. Synchronous speed. Slip.
Equivalent circuit per phase.
Torque-speed curve.
Nameplate: Rated parameters.
Construction. Principle of operation (Synchronous machine, Three-phase alternator).
Equivalent circuit per phase. Synchronous impedance.
Voltage regulation.
Nameplate: Rated parameters.

assessment_methods.method: Resolution and submission of individual activities (AE3)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.80 * Written Final Exam (AE1) + 0.1 * Laboratory Practical Activities (AE2) + 0.1 * Individual Activity Submissions (AE3), provided AE1 is 5 points or higher. If AE1 is less than 5 points, the final grade is 0.80 * AE1. For AE1 to be passed, both its problem-solving and theoretical/practical questions parts must meet minimum scores, and the overall AE1 score must be 5 or higher. AE2 and AE3 require a minimum of 5 points to contribute, are non-recoverable, and if the minimum is not met, they contribute 0 points to the final grade.
